column1: #! schema = 1
# What we currently CLAIM for each official conformance suite.
# Two rates per suite, never one. A blended figure would reward rejecting
# things: a parser that returns Err unconditionally scores 188/283 = 66% on
# JSONTestSuite while parsing nothing. See crates/core-verify/src/conformance.rs.
#   accept  = valid inputs correctly accepted   (y_* / no `error` marker)
#   reject  = invalid inputs correctly rejected (n_* / `error` marker present)
# Implementation-defined cases (JSONTestSuite's i_*) are measured and published
# but never gated: the spec permits either answer.
# THIS FILE RATCHETS ONE WAY. Raising a threshold is a normal reviewed change.
# Lowering one requires a [NEEDS-AYUSH-APPROVAL] header and sign-off (§8), and
# golden-guard covers this path.
# `unrecorded` is an ERROR, not a free pass. A conformance rate is
# deterministic — unlike a benchmark baseline, which may honestly be
# `uncalibrated` because timings are machine-dependent (ADR-006) — so
# `unrecorded` means no claim has been made yet, which is exactly the state
# konflux M1 is in before a parser exists.
# suite            class   rate
# Recorded 2026-08-08 from the measured result of the first JSON parser
# (crates/core-formats/src/json.rs). 95/95 and 188/188 — a perfect score on both
# classes, so the ratchet is now at its ceiling and any regression fails.
json-test-suite    accept  1.0
json-test-suite    reject  1.0
# Recorded 2026-08-08 from the first YAML parser. The two numbers say very
# different things and that is the point of never blending them:
#   accept 1.0  — every valid document in the suite is accepted, which is what
#                 K1 and konflux's usefulness depend on.
#   reject      — raised from 1.1% to 18.1% on 2026-08-09 by four families of
#                 rule: block scalar indicators, comment separation, anchor
#                 placement, and directive/document-marker structure. Each is
#                 unambiguous from the token stream. The rest of yaml-test-suite's
#                 must-reject cases need block/flow context tracking, which
#                 arrives with semantic_view at M2.
# A tab-indentation rule was tried and removed: it rejected 12 documents the
# suite calls valid. Rejecting valid input is the worse error — a refused file is
# one konflux cannot help with at all.
# GATE: the reject rate must rise substantially before M3 ships a merge.
# Structurally merging a document we failed to recognise as invalid is precisely
# the "silently wrong" failure §0 ranks first. Recorded in MILESTONES.
yaml-test-suite    accept  1.0
yaml-test-suite    reject  0.18
